reasoning: The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files including the critical PKGBUILD and found standard -bin packaging practices: sources pinned with SHA-256 checksums from legitimate upstream GitHub releases, no top-level code execution, prepare() only extracts tarballs, package functions install files and create standard wrapper scripts. No obfuscated code, unexpected network requests, or injection patterns detected. The inconclusive verdicts from other models were caused by API/tool errors (HTTP 400, JSONDecodeError), not security concerns.
disagreement_analysis: Two models (qwen and openrouter/free) failed to complete PKGBUILD audits due to API errors (HTTP 400 BadRequestError and JSONDecodeError respectively), forcing inconclusive verdicts. The deepseek model successfully audited all files and found no security issues. The disagreement stems from tool failures rather than substantive security analysis differences.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to audit PKGBUILD and .gitignore due to HTTP 400 API errors
openrouter/free model failed to audit PKGBUILD due to JSONDecodeError and only reviewed 1 of 7 files
learnings: Implement retry logic or fallback models when API errors occur during critical file audits (especially PKGBUILD)
Distinguish tool/API errors from security inconclusiveness in verdict reporting to avoid false uncertainty
The initial PKGBUILD top-level audit provides valuable signal even when full file review fails - this should be weighted more heavily in final verdicts
Models should be configured with higher timeout/retry limits for large files like PKGBUILD to prevent HTTP 400 errors
